quests.instruction: You entered a drawing contest and are waiting to hear the results. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing for good news about something you worked hard on can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing for good news about something you worked on gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Entering a contest is already a brave and creative step, no matter the final result!

quests.instruction: You cannot stop thinking about a hard conversation you need to have with a friend. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Thinking ahead about something difficult you need to say can keep your mind restless.
quests.explanation: Thinking ahead about something difficult you need to say can give you a restless, unsettled feeling.
quests.funFact: Planning out a few kind words ahead of time can help this restless feeling feel more manageable.

quests.instruction: You have practiced your dive so many times that you know exactly what to do. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Knowing your body remembers exactly what to do can make you feel sure and steady.
quests.explanation: Knowing your body remembers exactly what to do makes you feel sure and steady inside.
quests.funFact: Athletes call this feeling being 'in the zone' — it comes from lots of steady practice!

quests.instruction: You are lying in a hammock with nothing you need to do. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Having nowhere to rush to and nothing you need to fix can feel quietly good.
quests.explanation: Having nowhere to rush to and nothing you need to fix gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Giving your body a little unhurried rest time is good for both your mind and your muscles!

quests.instruction: You cannot get the jar lid to open no matter how hard you twist. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Struggling with something that will not budge can make your hands feel tense.
quests.explanation: Struggling with something that will not budge can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Running the lid under warm water is a trick that can help stubborn jars open more easily!

quests.instruction: You are waiting to see if your paper airplane design will win the contest. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing your own creation will do well can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing your own creation will do well gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Adjusting the wings just slightly can change how far and how straight a paper airplane flies!

quests.instruction: You keep replaying an awkward moment from earlier in your head. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Thinking about the same moment over and over can keep your mind feeling restless.
quests.explanation: Thinking about the same moment over and over can give you a restless, unsettled feeling.
quests.funFact: Talking it through with someone you trust can help a replaying thought quiet down.

quests.instruction: You have studied hard all week and know you are ready for the test. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Feeling well-prepared for something important can make you walk in with your head held high.
quests.explanation: Feeling well-prepared for something important makes you feel sure and ready to do your best.
quests.funFact: Studying a little bit every day, instead of all at once, helps this sure feeling grow steadily!

quests.instruction: You are watching the sunset after a simple, good day. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Looking back on an easy, pleasant day can leave you with a quiet, settled feeling.
quests.explanation: Looking back on an easy, pleasant day leaves you with a quiet, settled, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Noticing small good moments in your day is a simple way to feel this way more often!

quests.instruction: You have tried five times to solve the same math problem and keep getting it wrong. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Trying again and again without success can make you want to put your pencil down hard.
quests.explanation: Trying again and again without success can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Taking a short break and coming back can often help your brain find a fresh way to solve it.

quests.instruction: You are waiting to hear if your team made the finals. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing for good news while you wait can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing for good news while you wait gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: This wishing feeling can also help teams stay motivated as they wait for results!

quests.instruction: You keep imagining everything that could go wrong on tomorrow's class trip. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Picturing many small worries about a trip before it happens can feel restless.
quests.explanation: Picturing many small worries about something before it happens can give you a restless feeling.
quests.funFact: Packing your bag the night before can help settle a few of these worries early!

quests.instruction: You know your times tables so well that you can answer without even thinking. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Knowing something so well that the answers come easily can make you feel sure of yourself.
quests.explanation: Knowing something so well that answers come easily makes you feel sure and capable.
quests.funFact: Facts you practice often move into a part of your brain that remembers them almost instantly!

quests.instruction: You are relaxing on the porch after finishing all your chores. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Resting after finishing everything you needed to do can feel quietly satisfying.
quests.explanation: Resting after finishing everything you needed to do gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Finishing tasks before you rest can make the rest afterward feel even more enjoyable!

quests.instruction: You keep dropping the ball during practice no matter how hard you try. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Trying your hardest and still not getting it right can make you want to stomp your foot.
quests.explanation: Trying your hardest and still not succeeding can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Coaches say this feeling often shows up right before a big skill finally clicks into place!

quests.instruction: You wrote to your favorite author and are waiting for a reply. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing for a reply from someone you admire can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing for a reply from someone you admire gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Many authors love hearing from readers, even if a reply sometimes takes a little while!

quests.instruction: You have to give a speech next week and cannot stop thinking about it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Thinking about something far off, again and again, can keep your mind restless.
quests.explanation: Thinking about something coming up, over and over, can give you a restless, unsettled feeling.
quests.funFact: Practicing a little bit each day, instead of all at once, can help this restless feeling shrink.

quests.instruction: You have ridden your bike on this trail so many times that you know every turn. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Knowing a path so well that you do not need to think about it can make you feel sure and steady.
quests.explanation: Knowing a path so well that you do not need to think about it makes you feel sure and steady.
quests.funFact: Your brain builds a kind of map after enough practice, helping familiar paths feel easy!

quests.instruction: You are playing quietly with your favorite toy with nowhere you need to be. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Slow, unhurried play with something familiar can feel quietly satisfying.
quests.explanation: Slow, unhurried play with something familiar gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Quiet, unhurried play is a great way for your mind to rest even while your hands stay busy!

quests.instruction: Your kite will not stay up no matter how many times you try. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Trying the same thing over and over without it working can feel very stuck.
quests.explanation: Trying the same thing again and again without it working can give you a frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Running with the kite on a slightly windier day can make a big difference!

quests.instruction: You are waiting to hear back after trying out for the choir. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing for good news after doing your best can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing for good news after trying your best gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Trying out for something already shows courage, no matter what the answer turns out to be!

quests.instruction: You keep checking to make sure you packed everything for camp, again and again. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Double and triple-checking something important can be a sign your mind feels unsettled.
quests.explanation: Double and triple-checking something important can be a sign your mind feels restless and unsettled.
quests.funFact: Making a simple checklist ahead of time can help this restless feeling feel much calmer.

quests.instruction: You have solved this kind of math problem many times before and know just how to start. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Recognizing a problem you have solved many times before can make you feel sure of yourself.
quests.explanation: Recognizing a problem you have solved many times before makes you feel sure and ready.
quests.funFact: The more times you practice a skill, the faster and surer your brain gets at using it!

quests.instruction: You are sitting with your pet, enjoying a calm evening at home. How do you feel?
quests.hint: A quiet evening with a pet you love can feel simply, gently good.
quests.explanation: A quiet evening spent with a pet you love gives you a simple, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Spending calm time with a pet can help both you and your pet feel more relaxed!

quests.instruction: Your shoelace keeps coming undone every time you tie it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: The same small problem happening over and over can feel really stuck and annoying.
quests.explanation: The same small problem happening again and again can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: A double-knot is a simple trick that can help solve this exact problem for good!

quests.instruction: You are watching the sky, waiting for the clouds to clear for the picnic. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Wishing the weather will turn out just right can give you a light, waiting feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing the weather will turn out just right gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Clouds often clear up faster than expected — checking the sky is a fun way to watch it happen!

quests.instruction: You cannot stop thinking about your recital even hours before it starts. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Having your mind circle back to something important over and over can feel restless.
quests.explanation: Having your mind circle back to something important, again and again, can give you a restless feeling.
quests.funFact: A short walk or some slow stretching can help a busy, restless mind settle down a little.

quests.instruction: You have practiced your song so much that you cannot wait to perform it. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Knowing every note by heart can make you feel ready to step out and shine.
quests.explanation: Knowing every note by heart makes you feel sure and ready to step out and shine.
quests.funFact: Musicians say hours of practice are what turn nervous energy into this sure, ready feeling!

quests.instruction: You just tucked into a cozy blanket on a rainy afternoon. How do you feel?
quests.hint: Being warm and cozy with nowhere to be can feel quietly good inside.
quests.explanation: Being warm and cozy with nowhere to be gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Cozy, unhurried moments like this are a favorite comfort for people of every age!

quests.instruction: Your block tower falls down every time you get to the top three blocks. How do you feel?
quests.hint: The same setback happening at the exact same point each time can feel stuck and annoying.
quests.explanation: The same setback happening at the same point each time can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Building a wider base at the bottom is a clever trick that can help a tall tower stay steady!
